title: Building a 3-year revenue model
explanation: Startups and analysts build **models**: small spreadsheets that forecast revenue and profit from a few assumptions. The golden rule: put every **input** (an assumption you type) on its own sheet, and make everything else a **formula** that points at it. Then changing one assumption updates the whole model. This one is a subscription meal-kit startup.

tasks.prompt: Look at the Assumptions sheet: every input lives there. Back on Model, in B2, point Year 1's customers at the starting customers: =Assumptions!B2.
tasks.teach: Never type an assumption straight into a formula, like `=500*15`. If it lives in one cell, you can change it once and the whole model follows. Analysts call these **inputs**, and everything else **calculations**.
hints: Point at the other sheet: Assumptions!B2.

tasks.prompt: In C2, grow customers by the growth rate: =B2*(1+Assumptions!$B$3). Copy it to D2.
hints: Last year × (1 + growth). Lock the growth cell.
tasks.answer: =B2*(1+Assumptions!$B$3) in C2, then copy to D2

tasks.prompt: In B3:D3, work out yearly revenue: customers × monthly price × 12.
hints: Then copy it across to D3.
tasks.answer: =B2*Assumptions!$B$4*12 in B3, then copy across to D3

tasks.prompt: In B4:D4, work out variable costs: revenue × the cost percentage.
tasks.answer: =B3*Assumptions!$B$5 in B4, then copy across to D4

tasks.prompt: In B5:D5, point each year's fixed costs at the Assumptions sheet.
tasks.answer: =Assumptions!$B$6 in B5, then copy across to D5

tasks.prompt: In B6:D6, work out profit: revenue − variable costs − fixed costs.
hints: Then copy it across. Year 1 loses money, then it turns profitable.
tasks.answer: =B3-B4-B5 in B6, then copy across to D6

tasks.prompt: Last one: test the model. On the Assumptions sheet, change growth to 0.5 (50%). Every year updates by itself.
hints: Click the Assumptions tab, then type 0.5 in B3.
Then look back at Model: Year 3's profit jumps.

recap: Keep inputs on their own sheet, and make everything else formulas that point at them. Then one change to an assumption flows through the whole model.
